subject.title: fix: tighten findSchema.limit from Type.Number to Type.Integer with execution guard

question: Should the built-in find tool intentionally reject fractional limit values at both the model-facing schema and execution boundaries while retaining zero and negative normalization?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically sound, but changing an existing model-facing tool parameter from number to integer deliberately removes previously accepted input and therefore requires ownership of the compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Accept integer-only limits
options.body: Refresh the branch, confirm focused checks, and merge the narrow contract tightening because result counts are inherently integral and non-positive behavior remains compatible.

options.title: Preserve permissive input
options.body: Keep Type.Number and define an explicit rounding or truncation policy if fractional callers must continue working.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Leave the current contract unchanged until observed fractional callers or a broader built-in-tool numeric policy justify coordinated tightening.

recommendation.title: Accept integer-only limits
recommendation.body: Refresh the branch, confirm focused checks, and merge the narrow contract tightening because result counts are inherently integral and non-positive behavior remains compatible.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent numeric-contract work makes this the strongest available owner for deciding whether the model-facing compatibility change is intentional.
